brief: A worm's-eye hyperreal view up a capsule apartment tower, with its stacked concrete-and-steel modules each pierced by a single round porthole window. They recede in steep perspective against a pale overcast sky. Weather streaks, rust bleeding from bolts, peeling caulk and tiny curtains in a few windows are drawn with relentless precision. The medium is graphite pencil and fine technical pen hatching in cool neutral greys, with one restrained wash of faded mint and putty on the capsule panels. The light is flat and diffuse. The mood is clinical and slightly melancholic, and the rhythm is modular repetition fracturing into perspective.

A hyperreal streambed seen from just above the water: moss-furred stones, ivy tendrils trailing into the current, and a dropped garnet ring caught between two pebbles. The detail is obsessive, every frond and wet glint accounted for, as in a Millais riverbank. Build it in many thin transparent watercolour glazes over a luminous ground, layering viridian, madder lake, ultramarine and gamboge until the colour turns jewel-deep, then sharpen with hard coloured pencil for veins of leaves and the facets of the stone. The light is clear and even. The frame is crowded edge to edge with no empty air.

A hyperreal close study of a dried riverbed, its mud split into polygonal plates with curling edges, seen at dusk and drenched in indigo. Like cassava-paste resist on adire cloth, the crack lines and plate rims stay pale and almost unpainted. The plates themselves are saturated deep indigo, Prussian blue and blue-black, with mottled tie-dye blooms. Build the colour with fine spray misting and wet-in-wet watercolour, letting the reserved paper do the drawing. Pencil adds grit and pebble detail in the cracks. The view is top-down and the cracks spread edge to edge. It feels cool, dense and textile-like while remaining photographically convincing.

Trompe-l'oeil, viewed straight down: a brass pocket compass and a stub of beeswax candle rest on a creased, foxed parchment map. The paper's fold valleys, tea stains, pinholes and charred, torn edges are rendered so convincingly they seem lift-able. Use stained sepia, raw umber and faded madder watercolour washes for the aged paper, and fine dip-pen lines for coastlines, a dotted route and a red X. Use charcoal smudge for the burnt margins. The compass casts a real soft shadow across the drawn sea and its glass dome mirrors a window. The whole sheet fills the frame.

A tall, narrow hyperreal portrait of an eroded limestone slab, filling the whole vertical format like a monument photographed head-on. Faint carved glyph registers are half-dissolved under rosettes of grey-green and orange lichen. Low raking dawn light from the left throws every chisel scar and pit into relief. Render the stone in charcoal-like mass for the deep recesses and burnished graphite pencil for the sunlit planes, with only small touches of lichen colour in raw sienna and sage watercolour. The surface should feel cold and gritty, almost tactile. The palette stays near-monochrome and the composition stays rigidly frontal.

A vintage mint-green Vespa parked on a cobbled lane, split into two visual registers like an animation cel over a painted background. The background of shopfronts and awnings is soft and atmospheric, washed in hazy watercolour ochres and dove greys. The scooter in the foreground is hyperreal yet hard-edged, with flat opaque marker fills, one crisp shadow tone and one highlight tone per surface. Every contour is traced in a clean, even ink line. Its chrome is reduced to sharp graphic reflection shapes that are still photographically accurate. The contrast between the soft world and the crisp object is the point.

A hand reaches straight toward the viewer, fingers foreshortened enormously and palm creases sharp. It is drawn in detailed pen hatching and printed twice in slight offset, once in scarlet and once in cyan, so every contour doubles with a stereoscopic shimmer. The fingertips are offset widely and the wrist nearly converges, implying deep space. The ground is plain newsprint grey. Overlaps go to dark violet-black. Confrontational, optical and vertiginous.

A wren mid-song, beak open and throat feathers puffed, perched at the left edge and painted with photographic detail in fine pencil and watercolour. Behind it, the song unfolds horizontally as a spectrogram. Flow-field hatching streaks rightward in bands of magma colour, deep indigo to crimson to molten yellow, and bright chirps flare as vertical spikes and rising sweeps. The bird is warm brown realism and the sound field is pure luminous data. Lyrical and scientific.

Two small children's hands clasped in a lap of dark velvet, rendered as a daguerreotype. Silvery graphite in cool pewter and mercury greys gives the image a mirrored, metallic depth. Soft charcoal smudging forms the oval vignette, which shades into blue-violet tarnish halos and a brassy mat edge. Every knuckle crease and fingernail is exact, with a faint ghostly doubling where a hand moved during the long exposure. Grave, tender and archival.

A vast, extremely wide seascape with the horizon pressed low in the frame. The sun has nearly vanished, leaving a single emerald sliver flaring above a razor-flat sea. Soft spray gradients fade the sky from apricot through rose to steel blue overhead. Below, the water is built from thousands of tiny horizontal pen ticks in slate and pewter, catching faint coppery reflections. The green flash itself is a minuscule, intensely saturated spot, almost lost in the scale. Silent, held-breath, meteorological precision.

A silver salver crowded with pastel-iced petits fours, sugared violets and piped buttercream scrolls, set on a paper lace doily. Soft chalky masses of colour (shell pink, pistachio, powder blue, lilac and pale gold) are blended to velvety realism, with fine pencil cutting every swag, rosette and glossy fondant reflection. The composition curls in an asymmetric C-scroll, with crumbs scattered like ornament. Frothy, flirtatious and confectionery-perfect.

A beaten-up canvas sneaker on blue-lined notebook paper, drawn with obsessive outsider intensity in cheap blue ballpoint alone. Relentless cross-hatching and scribbled tonal masses push it to photographic realism: frayed laces, mud cracks, a split rubber toe cap. The surrounding margins are crammed with compulsive repeating loops, tally marks and cramped pseudo-handwriting that crowds the object but never touches it. Pressure varies from ghostly to gouged. Feverishly devoted, raw and handmade.

Tortoiseshell reading glasses rest on an open hardback beside a sunlit window, rendered in razor-sharp focus. The world beyond dissolves into overlapping soft discs of daylight: sage, lime, buttercream and sky blue, laid as wet watercolour circles with gentle haloed edges. In the foreground, precise graphite and coloured pencil capture lens reflections, a hinge screw and the fibrous paper of the pages. Shallow depth of field drives the whole image. Calm, studious, Sunday-morning.

A freshly sawn tree stump seen from above, its growth rings rendered with agate-like banding. Translucent watercolour glazes ripple concentrically in honey, caramel, rust, cream and smoky grey-brown. Saw marks, sap beads and radial cracks are drawn in fine pencil, and the rough bark collar frames the cut like an agate's crust. The rings are slightly off-centre and wavering, recording old droughts. Moss creeps in at one edge. Meditative and geological.

An overhead view of folded wool sweaters stacked edge to edge, filling the frame and forming a Diamond-in-a-Square quilt. Each sweater is a field of solid, sober colour: aubergine, deep teal, cranberry, bottle green and near-black. Flat alcohol-marker passes lay down the grounds, then tight coloured-pencil strokes rebuild every cable knit, pilled fibre and stray thread with tactile realism. Even north light, no cast drama, crisp seams where the garments meet. Severe geometry and plain colour meet a nearly touchable softness. Quiet, disciplined, domestic.

A vintage car hubcap filling the frame, its convex chrome holding a fisheye reflection of a sunny suburban street: lawns, clapboard houses, a bending sky and a tiny distorted figure of the viewer. Crisp black ink defines the hard specular breaks, and soft spray builds the smooth gradients from sky blue to asphalt grey. Bright cadmium and turquoise reflections are bent into curving bands. Road grime and tiny pits mark the rim. Sharp, sunny, nostalgic Americana.

A close frontal view of a shipping container's corrugated door, its locking bars and padlock eaten by rust. Layered spray, splatter and charcoal-like scumbles in burnt orange, iron oxide red, raw sienna and flaking teal paint build crusty, blistered realism. Drips of rust stain run down from each bolt, and stencilled cargo numbers peel half away. Vertical corrugations march across the frame in rhythmic shadow. Gritty, industrial, salt-weathered.

A scuffed vintage microphone on a chrome stand, its cable coiled on black stage boards, isolated in a hard-edged circle of follow-spot light. Everything outside the circle is dense, velvety charcoal black. Inside, the boards show gaffer tape, scuff marks and dust in the beam, with a faint haze rendered by soft spray. The light is cold white tinged pale amber at the rim. The circle sits low and slightly right, leaving vast dark above. Expectant, theatrical and lonely.

A paper crane half unfolded and flattened onto pale graph paper, its crease pattern now exposed as a web of valley and mountain lines. Crisp technical pen draws the creases, and soft pencil shading gives each facet its own tilt toward a cool window light. The washi is a warm kraft with visible fibres. Faint ghost folds remain where the paper refuses to flatten. Analytical, precise and contemplative.

An extreme close crop of a city pigeon's neck and shoulder, its feathers shimmering with mother-of-pearl iridescence. Densely burnished coloured pencil layers soft amethyst, seafoam green, rose and silvery slate until the surface glows, each barb rendered individually. A beady orange eye and the pale cere sit at the upper edge. The background is soft concrete grey. Pearly, delicate and unexpectedly regal.
